commit.message:
Forward CAPI assignment context to VS Code core telemetry (#326273)

* Forward CAPI assignment context to VS Code core telemetry

Add a proposed API scode.env.setTelemetryExperimentProperty that
allows trusted built-in extensions to set experiment properties on
VS Code's core telemetry pipeline.

The Copilot extension uses this to forward capi.assignmentcontext
(received via X-Copilot-Experiment and x-copilot-api-exp-assignment-context
response headers from CAPI) so that it appears on all VS Code telemetry
events, not just the Copilot extension's own events.

Flow:
1. CAPI responds with experiment headers
2. Copilot extension extracts them into serverExperiments
3. TelemetryService.setSharedProperty('capi.assignmentcontext', value)
4. Override forwards to vscode.env.setTelemetryExperimentProperty()
5. MainThreadTelemetry calls ITelemetryService.setExperimentProperty()
6. Property appears on all subsequent VS Code telemetry events

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: resolve CI failures - eslint and Copilot typecheck

- Remove 'VS Code' from proposed API JSDoc (eslint vscode-dts-vscode-in-comments rule)
- Use type assertion for proposed API call in Copilot extension to avoid
  TS2339 since the extension's tsconfig doesn't include proposed .d.ts files

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: replace 'as any' with typed Record cast for eslint compliance

- Use Record<string, unknown> instead of 'as any' to satisfy no-explicit-any
- Narrow API JSDoc to per-window scope (matching existing TAS pattern)

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Few updates

commit.message:
Fix agent host MCP server state and add per-server diagnostics (#326384)

* Fix agent host MCP server state and add per-server diagnostics

Discovered MCP servers were seeded as `Starting` before any SDK had
attempted to start them, and failures were only visible as a coarse
status. This corrects the lifecycle state and adds diagnostics.

- Seed `makeMcpServerCustomization` as `Stopped` instead of `Starting`;
  a declared-but-unstarted server has not begun connecting.
- The Copilot SDK emits no live "starting" signal on initial connect
  (servers settle inside a blocking init phase and `rpc.mcp.list`
  blocks until settled), so drive `Starting` optimistically from the
  workbench at the two real start triggers: sending a message
  (`_markEnabledMcpServersStarting`) and the disable->enable flip.
  Added `McpCustomizationController.markStarting` (skips
  Ready/AuthRequired/Starting).
- Log structured MCP lifecycle records (loaded/statusChanged/inventory)
  through the agent host's existing OTLP log stream with `OtelData`
  attributes, deduplicated by SDK status; failures log at error with
  the failure detail preserved in `McpServerErrorState`.
- Give each `(session, MCP server)` its own hidden Output channel that
  records lifecycle transitions; "Show Output" reveals it.
- Encapsulate the channel: `showMcpServerLog(sessionResource, serverId)`
  resolves and reveals internally; removed `logOutputChannelId` from the
  public `IAgentHostMcpServer` surface and the now-dead
  `getLogOutputChannelId` provider plumbing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address PR review: reliable MCP diagnostics + optimistic Start fixes

- Record MCP diagnostics from state-change events over a tracked set of
  sessions rather than as a side effect of `getMcpServers`, so a failure
  and a later recovery are both captured even without a UI re-query.
- Key the per-server log registry by the full session resource plus the
  raw customization id (not the UI-facing scoped id, whose authority is
  empty for Agents-window resources and would mix histories across
  sessions).
- Use an injective, filesystem-safe channel id (SHA1 hex of the composite
  key) so distinct servers can't collapse onto one logger/dedup entry.
- Dispose each session's loggers and Output channel registrations when the
  session goes away (session dispose / removal / provisional backend swap),
  fixing the logger/file-handle leak.
- Route the explicit Start/Restart (`startMcpServer`) through `markStarting`
  so it shows Starting during the SDK's blocking reconnect, and always
  reconcile via a trailing inventory refresh (try/finally) so a rejected
  enable can't leave the UI stuck at Starting -- same fix applied to the
  enable path in `_reconcileMcpServerEnablement`.
- Add coverage for the explicit-start optimistic Starting behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix CI: stub ILoggerService/IOutputService in customization service test

The MCP diagnostics registry now resolves `ILoggerService`/`IOutputService`
lazily when `record` runs (via the new eager state recording). The
enablement unit test instantiated the abstract service against a bare
`TestInstantiationService`, so `getMcpServers` threw
`this._loggerService.createLogger is not a function`. Stub both services
(NullLoggerService + a minimal IOutputService) in the test harness.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: hide worktree/branch config when folder has no usable git repo (#326396)

The new-session repository controls (isolation "New Worktree" and "Branch")
were rendered but disabled when the selected folder had no usable git
repository. Show nothing instead of a dead, greyed-out control.

- Agent Host provider: skip the isolation control at render time when the
  resolved schema offers no `worktree` option (non-git folder). The filter
  runs before the desktop/mobile `_shouldRenderProperty` overrides so the
  mobile-aware subclass (also used on desktop) cannot reintroduce it.
- Copilot Chat provider: make `SessionHasGitRepositoryContext` HEAD-commit
  aware and reactive, so an empty repository (repo object exists, no
  commits) counts as "no usable git repo" — matching CopilotCLISession's
  own worktree gating. Gate both the Isolation and Branch new-session
  actions on that key via `when` (Branch moved from `precondition`, which
  only disabled it, to `when`, which hides it).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix new cloud session disappearing and misgrouping after commit (#326230)

* Fix new cloud session disappearing and misgrouping after commit

The Agents window (vs/sessions) drove a new cloud (RemoteNewSession) agent
session through the wrong commit path, causing it to disappear ~5s after
delegating, and then group under "Unknown" / flip its repo label once it did
appear. Three related fixes:

1. Wait for the committed resource on cloud sessions. A cloud session commits
   a new resource mid-request (untitled -> /task/<id>), like Copilot CLI, so
   _sendFirstChat now routes RemoteNewSession through _waitForCommittedSession
   instead of waiting on the stale untitled resource (which timed out and
   removed the session). The wait is also deferred (skips the response-complete
   race, longer timeout) because the cloud commit is delayed by a confirmation
   round-trip and network delegation.

2. Attach owner/name metadata to PR-less task cards so a freshly created task
   groups under its repo instead of "Unknown"/"Other" until a PR resolves.
   Repo identity is hoisted from PullArtifactRef.repo to CloudSessionData.repo
   (a task has a repo regardless of a pull artifact); resolvePullArtifact now
   takes repo as an explicit argument.

3. Consolidate the repo label. Both the new-session workspace and the committed
   session adapter now derive an owner/repo label via a shared
   githubRemoteRepoLabel helper, so a cloud session stays in the same group
   before and after commit (no more microsoft/vscode -> vscode flip).

Adds a regression test for the cloud commit-swap.

commit.message:
fix: mitigate Linux webview renderer FD exhaustion during resource loading (#326272)

Codex extension surfaced a renderer forced exit after hitting EMFILE on Linux
when a webview issued very large number of concurrent local resource fetches.

Diagnosis
- Codex extension can trigger roughly 625 concurrent webview resource requests.
- Webview resource loading currently forwards each request to the host and
  begins transferring the returned body immediately.
- Disk reads are chunked at 256 KiB, and Mojo uses shared-memory FDs for
  payloads above 64 KiB, so each in-flight resource body can consume file
  descriptors in the renderer while it is being streamed.
- The sandboxed renderer runs with RLIMIT_NOFILE=1024 on Linux.
- This is not specific to codex extensionn, any extension with enough concurrent
  resource bodies can accumulate to exhaust the renderer FD budget.

This makes the problem specifically about the number of simultaneously active
host-backed response bodies. A naive limiter around WebviewElement.loadResource()
would not address the root cause because loadResource() returns as soon as the
stream is transferred, while the FD pressure persists for the lifetime of the
stream in the renderer.

Introduce a service-worker-side global concurrency limit for host-backed webview
resource response bodies.

- Add a global limit of 32 active host-backed resource bodies in the webview
  service worker.
- Acquire a permit before creating/posting the load-resource request so time
  spent waiting for a slot does not consume the existing 30 second
  RequestStore timeout.
- Hold the permit for the full lifetime of the returned ReadableStream, and
  release it only when the stream reaches EOF, errors, or is cancelled.
- Release exactly once on all non-stream results and on every early/error path,
  including timeout handling.
- Preserve existing range request behavior, ETag/304 handling, CacheStorage
  behavior, Safari fallback streaming, and cancellation semantics.
- For cacheable responses, keep the permit until both source transfer and the
  associated cache write complete, without delaying delivery of the response
  back to the webview.
- Bump the service worker version and WebviewElement expected version together
  so clients pick up the updated worker.

Tests
- Add an API integration regression test that creates a webview, materializes
  many local resources, fetches them concurrently from inside the webview, and
  verifies the webview stays alive and all loads complete.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Automations: remove lingering :has() selectors from dialog and list (#325864)

* Automations: remove lingering :has() selectors from dialog and list

Follow-up to #324986 / #324985, which removed the catastrophic
body:has(.automation-dialog) rules. The Automations UI still shipped four
:has() selectors in aiCustomizationManagement.css that add :has()
invalidation bookkeeping to the global stylesheet (present in Stable even
when the feature is off). This removes all of them:

- Chat-input chips (Configure Tools / Add Context / List MCP Servers) were
  hidden with .action-item:has(.action-label.codicon-*). .action-item
  is a workbench-wide anchor, so this was the one with Stable-wide reach.
  They are now hidden by targeting the .action-label codicon class
  directly. .action-item has no intrinsic box spacing, so the slot
  collapses to zero width and there is no visual gap. Known trade-off: the
  hidden chips stay in the toolbar's arrow-key focus rotation (the action
  bar skips only disabled/separator items). This is accepted for now; the
  dialog will migrate to newChatInput.ts, which never renders these
  MenuId.ChatInput chips.
- .automations-row:has(:focus-visible) -> .automations-row:focus-within,
  matching the sibling customization lists' documented focus-ring pattern.
- .automations-row-wrapper:has(> .automations-row-history) (x2) ->
  a JS-toggled .automations-row-wrapper-expanded class. The history panel
  is always in the DOM, so the old :has() matched every row; the class
  reflects the actual expanded state, which also restores hover highlight on
  collapsed rows and only flattens the card corners when expanded.

Scoped entirely to the automations CSS block; no shared components change.
Type-check, ESLint, and stylelint pass.

commit.message:
Don't leak internal cache_control sentinel to BYOK providers that can't consume it

The host injects an Anthropic cache-breakpoint (cache_control data part) into
tool results for every non-messages endpoint, including third-party providers
(Ollama, custom) that can't recognize it and serialize it verbatim into their
upstream request. Gate emission in convertToApiChatMessage so the sentinel only
reaches vendors whose converters handle it (anthropic, gemini, openrouter).

Fixes #313920

commit.message:
Gate default-to-Agent-Host-Copilot behind chat.defaultToCopilotHarness (#326265)

* Gate default-to-Agent-Host-Copilot behind chat.defaultToCopilotHarness

Follow-up to #326086, which made Agent Host Copilot the computed default
for editor and panel chat unconditionally whenever the agent host is
enabled. Add the experimental setting that should have gated it,
mirroring chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness.

- New chat.defaultToCopilotHarness setting (experimental, default false),
  registered next to the other agent-host chat settings.
- getComputedDefaultSessionType returns AgentHostCopilot only when the
  agent host is enabled AND the setting is opted in; every editor/panel
  caller routes through this one function, so the gate covers both
  surfaces. The one-time chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness migration swap
  stays independent, scoped to the Local -> Copilot migration.

Because the default is false and the agent host is enabled by default in
Insiders, first-time Insiders users now land on Local until the
experiment (or an explicit setting) turns it on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: refresh picker on the gate, keep migration test independent

- Add ChatConfiguration.DefaultToCopilotHarness to the
  SessionTypePickerActionItem config-change listener so the picker
  recomputes its provider ordering/labels when the setting changes at
  runtime, instead of showing stale order until an unrelated refresh.
- Revert the DefaultToCopilotHarness override in the preferCopilotHarness
  swap test so it keeps proving the one-time migration swaps Local ->
  Copilot solely because EditorPreferCopilotHarness is enabled, and fix
  the now-accurate afterApply comment.

commit.message:
Default editor and panel chat to Agent Host Copilot when the agent host is enabled (#326086)

* Default editor and panel chat to Agent Host Copilot when the agent host is enabled

Builds on the chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness behavior to make Agent Host
Copilot the computed default chat provider for both editor and panel chat
whenever the agent host is enabled, so first-time users land on Copilot instead
of Local. chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness stays scoped to the one-time
Local -> Copilot migration only.

- Thread an agentHostEnabled flag (from IAgentHostEnablementService) through the
  default-session-type resolution and its callers.
- Keep Local visible and selectable; honor explicit and remembered selections.
- New Local Chat opens a local session directly: it cancels the in-flight
  default-provider resolution (which would otherwise block on agent host
  activation) so the local request wins immediately.
- Open a Local chat first in all chat participant API tests, since chat
  participants are a Local-harness feature.
- Add a smoketest.openLocalChat command for Local panel smoke scenarios; the
  sandbox reopen path reveals the existing local session to avoid a focus race.
- Register an IAgentHostEnablementService stub in the component fixtures.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: honor resolved session type when starting a new chat

Fixes the New Chat drop bug (review comment #2 on #326086): when the
agent host is enabled the computed default is a non-local harness, so the
editor clear path recomputed that default and dropped explicit or
preserved local requests.

- clearChatSessionPreservingType now branches on the resolved session
  type for the sidebar (non-local -> loadSession, local ->
  startNewLocalSession) so a generic New Chat from a Local panel
  preserves Local, consistent with contributed panels.
- The resolved type is threaded through IChatWidget.clear ->
  viewOptions.clear -> chatEditor.clear -> clearChatEditor so the editor
  opens a session of that type instead of recomputing the default. This
  restores explicit "New Local Chat" from a non-local editor.
- clearChatEditor applies an explicit target type directly and keeps its
  swap-aware default only for direct (untargeted) calls.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: cancel the previous applyModel resolution before replacing it

Assigning a new CancellationTokenSource to the MutableDisposable only
disposes the previous source, and disposing a CancellationTokenSource
does not cancel it. So a re-entrant applyModel() (view render, switch
session) left the prior in-flight resolution running, racing to call
showModel with a stale result. Cancel the previous source explicitly
before replacing it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Prefer Copilot harness once for editor sessions (#326178)

* Prefer Copilot harness once for editor sessions

Add the `chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness` setting (replacing the
`chat.editor.defaultProvider` enum). When enabled, an existing local editor
chat session is swapped to the Agent Host Copilot CLI exactly once, guarded by
a persisted marker (CHAT_PREFERRED_COPILOT_HARNESS_STORAGE_KEY).

The one-time swap only fires when the agent host is enabled, since the Copilot
harness is otherwise unavailable. The setting has no other effect: it does not
change the computed default provider or editor session-type visibility for
fresh users, so leaving it off (the default) preserves today's behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix stale acquireDefaultNewSession doc comment

The comment referenced the `chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness` setting selecting
a provider, but that setting no longer drives the computed default. Describe the
actual behavior: acquire the computed default when it is non-local, else fall
back to a local session.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Apply the one-time preferCopilotHarness swap on the editor path

`resolveDefaultNewChatSessionType` set the migration marker as a side effect of
merely computing the type, so callers that discarded the result (notably the
editor New Chat path, which called `widget.clear()`) consumed the one-time swap
without ever applying it. The editor then stayed on Local, and the marker
blocked any future swap.

Make `resolveDefaultNewChatSessionType` pure: it returns
`{ sessionType, isPreferCopilotHarnessSwap }` and no longer writes the marker.
Callers persist the marker only when they actually apply the swap:

- The sidebar path in `clearChatSessionPreservingType` marks after loading the
  swapped session.
- `clearChatEditor` now resolves the swap for a local editor session, opens a
  Copilot editor, and marks it there instead of recomputing a swap-unaware
  default via `getDefaultNewChatSessionResource`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Voice agent always on streaming mode to support barge in (#326165)

* Fix voice barge-in protocol

Remove the unsupported outbound barge_in monitor messages and keep microphone streaming on the established PTT protocol. Clear playback suppression when PTT starts so backend VAD receives interruption audio immediately, while preserving the inbound barge_in playback cancellation event.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 7972bf67-b7f5-4937-9ea8-b1b9a9f13e0d

* Voice hands-free: stream mic during playback for backend barge-in

In hands-free mode, keep the mic streaming while the assistant speaks by
opening a passive, non-interrupting PTT turn (_startBargeInListen) reusing
the warm mic. This lets the backend's server-VAD hear the user talk over
the assistant and emit speech_started / barge_in (already wired to stop
TTS). If the user stays silent the turn simply becomes the next listening
turn once playback ends. Non-hands-free (manual PTT) keeps its prior
suppressUntil behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: e3a8372f-08f2-4a5b-bdf4-ed2a29be4622

* Voice hands-free: fix manual mic interrupt during passive barge-in listen

The passive barge-in turn opened during assistant playback previously set
`_pttToggleMode = true`. Pressing the mic button mid-playback then hit
`pttDown()`'s toggle branch, which sent `ptt_end` and finalized the turn
WITHOUT stopping playback — leaving the assistant talking and the manual
interrupt broken.

Track the passive listen with a dedicated `_bargeInListenActive` flag
instead. An explicit `pttDown()` now promotes that live stream into a
user-driven interrupt on the SAME turn (no second `ptt_start`, no mic
re-acquire): it stops playback, drops queued audio, opens the user turn,
re-anchors hold telemetry, and moves to listening. Releasing the button
flows through the normal `pttUp()` path.

If the user stays silent through playback, `onPlaybackStopped` converts
the passive turn into a normal tap-to-stop listening turn (toggle mode +
server-VAD auto-end). The flag is cleared in `_finishPtt()` and
`disconnect()` for hygiene.

Addresses the Copilot review comment on #326165.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: e3a8372f-08f2-4a5b-bdf4-ed2a29be4622

* Fix voice barge-in protocol

Remove the unsupported outbound barge_in monitor messages and keep microphone streaming on the established PTT protocol. Clear playback suppression when PTT starts so backend VAD receives interruption audio immediately, while preserving the inbound barge_in playback cancellation event.

Copilot-Session: 7972bf67-b7f5-4937-9ea8-b1b9a9f13e0d

* Voice hands-free: stream mic during playback for backend barge-in

In hands-free mode, keep the mic streaming while the assistant speaks by
opening a passive, non-interrupting PTT turn (_startBargeInListen) reusing
the warm mic. This lets the backend's server-VAD hear the user talk over
the assistant and emit speech_started / barge_in (already wired to stop
TTS). If the user stays silent the turn simply becomes the next listening
turn once playback ends. Non-hands-free (manual PTT) keeps its prior
suppressUntil behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: e3a8372f-08f2-4a5b-bdf4-ed2a29be4622

* Voice hands-free: fix manual mic interrupt during passive barge-in listen

The passive barge-in turn opened during assistant playback previously set
`_pttToggleMode = true`. Pressing the mic button mid-playback then hit
`pttDown()`'s toggle branch, which sent `ptt_end` and finalized the turn
WITHOUT stopping playback — leaving the assistant talking and the manual
interrupt broken.

Track the passive listen with a dedicated `_bargeInListenActive` flag
instead. An explicit `pttDown()` now promotes that live stream into a
user-driven interrupt on the SAME turn (no second `ptt_start`, no mic
re-acquire): it stops playback, drops queued audio, opens the user turn,
re-anchors hold telemetry, and moves to listening. Releasing the button
flows through the normal `pttUp()` path.

If the user stays silent through playback, `onPlaybackStopped` converts
the passive turn into a normal tap-to-stop listening turn (toggle mode +
server-VAD auto-end). The flag is cleared in `_finishPtt()` and
`disconnect()` for hygiene.

Addresses the Copilot review comment on #326165.

commit.message:
agentHost: fix subagent progress pill stuck 'in progress' race (#326169)

* agentHost: retry transient subscribe failures to fix subagent status desync

Fixes a race where a subagent's chat resource is referenced by an
action delivered to the client (toolCallStart/toolCallReady reporting
the subagent's chat URI) before the Agent Host has actually finished
registering that resource. The client's first subscribe attempt fails
with "Cannot subscribe to unknown resource", and because subagent
progress observation acquires its subscription exactly once at setup
time, the resulting error was never retried — leaving the subagent's
live status (and therefore its progress spinner / pill) stuck until
some unrelated caller happened to re-acquire the same subscription
(e.g. opening the subagent chat directly, which fetches state through
a separate path and thus showed the correct, completed state).

AgentSubscriptionManager.getSubscription now retries a bounded number
of times with a short backoff before giving up and surfacing the error,
absorbing this benign registration race without masking a genuinely
invalid resource for more than a few seconds.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326051

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: compute subagent chat URI on the server, not the client

Previously, clients derived a subagent-spawning tool call's chat URI
themselves via buildSubagentChatUri(session, toolCallId) as soon as
they recognized the tool call (via _meta.toolKind === 'subagent'),
duplicating logic the host already implements identically. Since the
host is authoritative for this deterministic naming scheme, it should
tell clients the URI directly instead of every client (re-)deriving it.

AgentSideEffects now stamps _meta.subagentChatUri onto a tool call's
ChatToolCallStart/Delta/Ready action as soon as toolKind is recognized
as 'subagent' — centralizing the computation in the one place all
providers (Copilot, Claude, Codex) funnel their actions through,
regardless of which action type first carries the toolKind hint
(Copilot sets it at Start, Claude at Ready).

Clients (getSubagentChatResource, _observeSubagentSession) now prefer
this server-provided URI, falling back to local computation only for
older/restored snapshots that predate this field.

readToolCallMeta's parameter type is widened from ToolCallState to a
minimal structural IHasToolCallMeta shape so it can also validate the
_meta bag on the wire actions themselves (not just persisted state),
keeping all _meta reads routed through the validating reader per the
local/code-no-untyped-meta-access lint rule.

This does not by itself fix the resource-registration race from
#326051 (the chat resource behind the URI is still created later, once
the agent SDK's own subagent_started signal arrives) — subscribers
still need the retry added separately in AgentSubscriptionManager. This
change removes the client-side URI duplication as requested, ahead of
that fix.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Revert "agentHost: retry transient subscribe failures to fix subagent status desync"

Superseded by a server-side fix: instead of the client retrying a
subscribe that raced the host's own resource registration, the host
will hold the subscribe request open until the subagent chat resource
is actually registered (or the spawn attempt definitively fails),
removing the race at its source rather than papering over it with
client-side retries.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: wait for a subagent chat to register instead of retrying client-side

Replaces the client-side subscribe retry with a server-side fix that
removes the race at its source: AgentService now tracks a subagent
chat resource as 'expected soon' the moment a tool call action reveals
_meta.subagentChatUri (stamped by AgentSideEffects), and a subscribe()
that races the resource's registration (which only happens once the
agent SDK confirms subagent_started and _onChatSpawned calls addChat)
waits for that registration instead of throwing 'Cannot subscribe to
unknown resource' immediately.

The wait is bounded by SUBAGENT_CHAT_PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS (15s, well
above the sub-second registration lag typically observed) so a
subscribe still surfaces an error - just later - if the tool call is
denied or cancelled before the subagent ever spawns.

Also fixes a latent, previously-masked bug in subscribe()'s fallback
chain: an unregistered subagent chat URI used to fall through to a
plain restoreSession(resource) call, treating the chat-shaped URI as
if it were a session URI. This path is now skipped entirely for
subagent chat URIs in favor of the pending-registration wait.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326051

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: trim comments to essentials

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: fix pending subagent chat check using wrong state accessor

getSessionState() resolves ANY chat URI (including subagent ones) to
its owning session's state, so it returned the parent session's
(already-registered) state for a not-yet-created subagent chat --
making _trackPendingSubagentChat always believe the resource was
already registered and skip creating a pending entry. subscribe()
then always fell through to the immediate 'unknown resource' error,
exactly as before the fix.

Use getSnapshot(), which looks up the chat URI directly in _chatStates
and correctly returns undefined until addChat() runs.

Confirmed via repro logs: previously, subscribe failed ~20ms after the
request with no wait, right around when session/chatAdded fired --
indicating the wait path was never actually taken.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: fix test using wrong state accessor for subagent chat check

Same bug as the previous commit, but in this test's own assertion:
getSessionState() resolves the subagent chat URI back to its already-
registered parent session, so the 'not registered yet' precondition
check was always false. Use getSnapshot() instead, matching the fix
in AgentService._trackPendingSubagentChat.

Verified locally (all now-runnable): agentSideEffects.test.ts (125
passing), agentService.test.ts (132 passing), agentSubscription.test.ts
(46 passing).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: address Copilot review feedback on pending subagent chat handling

- Don't arm the pending-registration timeout while a subagent tool
  call is still awaiting user confirmation. The wait is now armed only
  once the tool call is confirmed to run (ChatToolCallReady with
  confirmed set, or a later ChatToolCallConfirmed(approved: true)),
  so a slow user response can no longer cause a premature timeout that
  a later subagent_started can't revive.
- Resolve (never reject) the pending deferred on timeout, avoiding an
  unhandled promise rejection when no subscribe is in flight to
  observe it; subscribe() still surfaces the same unknown-resource
  error via the missing snapshot.
- Dispose and remove the fired timer's own map entry, fixing a
  leak where every subagent tool call that never spawns (denied,
  cancelled, or never confirmed) left its disposable retained for
  the process lifetime.
- Track pending subagent tool calls across whichever action first
  reveals _meta.subagentChatUri/toolKind, since providers stamp it at
  different points (Copilot at Start, Claude at Ready) and later
  actions for the same tool call don't repeat it.
- Added regression tests: a slow user confirmation no longer times
  out prematurely, denial cleans up without a dangling wait, and the
  adapter now asserts _meta.subagentChatUri wins over a discovery
  content block resource.

Verified locally: agentService.test.ts (134 passing),
agentSideEffects.test.ts + stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts (223 passing).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: refine chats list row rendering for quick chats

- Show the chat icon on the status icon (instead of a separate icon in
  the details row) only when it does not appear in the Chats section,
  where the section header already carries one
- Hide diff stats and relative timestamp from the sessions list rows
- Reduce the session row height, icon size and remove the second
  (details) line for quick-chat rows only; regular sessions keep the
  standard two-line row with full details (type icon, diff stats,
  status/description, timestamp)
- Suppress the InProgress "Working..." status text for quick chats,
  whose compact spinner status icon already conveys progress

  regardless of whether the row is in the default Chats section. The
  tree delegate reserves a fixed single-line height for every quick
  chat, so leaving the padding in place for non-Chats-section rows
  overflowed the reserved row height.

  top-aligned (matching desktop), instead of inheriting the phone
  layout's row-level vertical centering, which misaligned the status
  icon from the title when an approval/CI row grew the row taller.
- Remove the now-unused `in-chats-section` class toggle.

commit.message:
sessions: sync docked details panel min-width with sessions list, support sash-collapse (#326135)

sessions: sync docked details panel min-width with sessions list and support sash-collapse

When only the docked details view is shown (editor content hidden) in
single side-pane layout, its minimum width now matches the sessions
list's minimum width, and dragging the sash below that width collapses
(hides) the panel, mirroring the sessions list's own snap-to-hide
behavior.

- Export SESSIONS_LIST_MINIMUM_WIDTH from sidebarPart.ts as the shared
  minimum width source of truth.
- SinglePaneMainEditorPart now reports that minimum width, is a snap
  view, and resets to the detail panel's default width on double-click
  only while editor content is hidden (previously reset to 60% of the
  window, which is meant for the editor+chat split).
- SinglePaneWorkbench maps the grid's native sash-drag collapse/reveal
  of the shared node onto hiding/showing the auxiliary bar in that
  state.
- DockedAuxiliaryBarController disables its own overlay sash while
  editor content is hidden, since the real grid sash now owns
  resizing/collapsing there (avoids two competing sashes).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: add prompt timeline sticky header (#326080)

* sessions: add prompt timeline sticky header

Adds a flat, opaque "sticky prompt header" to the Agents window chat transcript, modelled on
the editor's sticky scroll: while you scroll it pins the current prompt to the top, names it with
an N/M position, and opens the prompt picker when selected so you can jump anywhere.

The timeline is now split into two independently toggleable surfaces, each backed by the
experimentation service and off by default:
- sessions.promptTimeline.rail — the scrollbar that fans into prompt pills on scroll/hover
- sessions.promptTimeline.stickyHeader — the sticky prompt header

Both reuse the shared PromptTimelineModel (new activeTick + activePinned observables) and the
existing "Go to Prompt..." picker. The former single sessions.promptTimeline.enabled setting is
removed in favour of the two surface settings, so rail-only, header-only, both, or neither all work.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: simplify prompt timeline setting descriptions

Tighten both setting descriptions to a single "Controls whether…" sentence
matching the house style, dropping the implementation detail.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: address prompt timeline sticky header review feedback

- derive the sticky label and N/M position from the unbucketed active prompt so long chats
  (over the rail's tick cap) report the real prompt and total, not a bucket representative
- rely on the native button for Enter/Space activation instead of a hand-rolled key handler
- fall back to the localized "(empty prompt)" label for attachment-only prompts
- suppress the band's drop shadow in high-contrast themes

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: prompt timeline UX improvements (#326023)

* sessions: prompt timeline rail becomes one scrollbar that fans in on scroll/hover

Reshape the prompt timeline into a single scrollbar lane instead of a pill
column sitting next to the transcript's native scrollbar. At rest it is a plain
scrollbar (the rail draws its own thumb and the transcript's native vertical
slider is hidden while the rail is active). On a deliberate gesture the thumb
recedes and the prompt pills fan in over the same lane with a macOS-dock style
fisheye:

- Hard/fast scroll (wheel-velocity gated, capture phase so it works mid-content
  not just at the scroll limits) blooms the fan centred on where you are, and it
  glides continuously with the viewport as you keep scrolling. The reveal is
  gated on a real scrollTop change, so flicking against the top/bottom limit -
  or programmatic virtualization nudges - never opens it.
- Hovering the lane blooms the fan and lets it follow the cursor; dragging the
  lane scrubs the transcript; clicking a pill still jumps; keyboard focus reveals
  the pills. It quietly collapses back to a plain scrollbar after a short linger
  once you stop scrolling and are not hovering.
- Pills are laid out as an evenly-spaced dock centred in the lane (stable under
  virtualization) rather than scattered by content position; the two-tone
  green/red diff decoration and the hover card are preserved.

Also reduces forced reflows on the hover/scroll paths (position the card and
lane from cached geometry instead of getBoundingClientRect) and avoids churning
the linger timer every scroll frame. Reduced-motion disables the fisheye but
still reveals the calm dock.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: address prompt timeline PR feedback

- normalize wheel deltas via StandardWheelEvent so line-mode devices trigger the fan
- keep the native scrollbar when the rail is too narrow (below MIN_HOST_WIDTH) to replace it
- use generic mouse listeners for lane scrub + mark guard so touch/iOS works
- track keyboard focus: reveal a calm dock (:focus-within) with the fisheye suppressed
- scale scrollTop into the estimated coordinate space before interpolating the fan focus
- map the thumb/scrub math onto the list viewport height (ScrollbarState-style)
- use --vscode-cornerRadius-circle for the thumb radius
- extract the hard-wheel detector into a named helper

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* distance update

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Codex agent: MCP tools + customizations parity (config pickup, auth, .agents, client plugins) (#325977)

* codex: launch workbench-configured MCP servers via -c overrides

The codex agent read back MCP servers that the app-server already knew from
the user's global ~/.codex/config.toml, but never told codex which servers to
run. Configure the app-server with the workbench's root `mcpServers` config
(the same source the Copilot agent forwards to its SDK) so those servers are
actually launched and their tools become usable.

- Add buildCodexMcpServerOverrides() in codexMcpServers.ts: converts the root
  mcpServers config into codex `-c mcp_servers.<name>={...}` TOML overrides,
  with a minimal TOML encoder and per-entry validation (maps headers ->
  http_headers, drops the workbench-only type discriminator, stringifies env,
  skips malformed entries and names codex cannot address in a -c key path).
- Wire _buildMcpServerOverrides() into the app-server spawn args in codexAgent.
- Add unit tests for the encoder/validation.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: surface .agents skills + hooks in the Customizations view

Codex natively discovers skills from the VS Code `.agents/skills` convention
(repo + user scope) and hooks from `.codex`, but the agent only surfaced MCP
servers to the workbench Customizations view. Enumerate codex's effective
skills and hooks via the cwd-scoped `skills/list` / `hooks/list` app-server
methods and project them into DirectoryCustomization containers so what codex
loaded is visible alongside the MCP servers.

- Add codexCustomizations.ts: pure mappers codexSkillsToContainers (grouped by
  scope, de-duped by path) and codexHooksToContainers (de-duped by key).
- getSessionCustomizations() appends the skill/hook containers (best-effort when
  the connection is ready); _materialize() pushes SessionCustomizationUpdated so
  the view refreshes once the app-server connection comes up.
- Add codexCustomizations.test.ts unit tests.

Verified end-to-end against the real codex binary: a repo `.agents/skills`
skill is reported by skills/list and surfaces as a Skill customization under
the Repository container.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: ingest client-pushed plugin customizations

The codex active-client customizations setter was a no-op, so client-pushed
("Open Plugin") customizations the workbench synced were dropped. Wire them up
the way the Copilot and Claude agents already do, adapted to codex's
process-global app-server:

- Materialize + parse each client plugin via the shared IAgentPluginManager +
  pluginParsers (same components Claude/Copilot use), stored per session in a
  new CodexClientCustomizationStore with a per-customization enablement overlay.
- Surface the plugins (with their skill/MCP/agent/instruction/hook children) in
  getSessionCustomizations and honor setCustomizationEnabled toggles.
- Feed each plugin's MCP servers per-session via thread/start.config.mcp_servers
  (verified against the real codex binary: the server starts for that thread
  only), so a plugin's server runs only for sessions that enable it.
- Feed each plugin's skills via the process-global skills/extraRoots/set as the
  union of enabled skill roots across live sessions (codex has no per-thread
  skill-roots knob; this matches the global nature of client plugin choices).

Inject IAgentPluginManager / IFileService / INativeEnvironmentService (already
registered where CodexAgent is created). Hooks and custom agents are surfaced
but not yet fed to codex.

Verified end-to-end against the real codex binary: a plugin's skills/extraRoots
skill appears in skills/list and its thread/start.config MCP server appears in
mcpServerStatus/list. Agents window boots and registers codex with the new deps.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: apply root MCP servers per-thread so config changes are picked up

The codex agent baked the workbench root `mcpServers` config into the
app-server's `-c mcp_servers.<name>=<toml>` spawn overrides. Because the
app-server is process-global and spawned once, servers added to Host
Settings after the app-server started were never applied (and the TOML
override key parser could not address names with dots/whitespace).

Move root `mcpServers` from the process-global spawn overrides to each
session's `thread/start.config.mcp_servers`, merged with that session's
enabled client-plugin servers. codex applies `config.mcp_servers` as
per-thread overrides that merge with the user's global
`~/.codex/config.toml`, so every new session now reflects the current
root config without restarting the shared app-server -- matching the
copilot agent's per-session model. A prewarmed-but-unused thread whose
MCP set changed before its first turn is restarted to pick up the new
servers (same mechanism already used for client tools).

Replaces the TOML string encoder with a JSON producer
(`codexMcpServersFromConfig` / `toCodexMcpServerJson`) since per-thread
config takes structured JSON; server names with dots/whitespace are now
valid (they are JSON object keys, not `-c` override key segments).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: log MCP server wiring + startup status for diagnosability

The per-thread MCP refactor dropped the "configuring N MCP servers" log,
leaving no signal for whether a workbench-configured server actually
reached codex or what state it settled into. Add three concise info
logs: the MCP server names passed at `thread/start`, each
`mcpServer/startupStatus/updated` transition (with any error), and the
post-refresh inventory (per-server state + tool count). This makes an
auth/connection failure of an http MCP server (e.g. an OAuth-gated
endpoint) visible in the agent host log instead of silently surfacing as
"no MCP servers" in the model's reply.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: authenticate OAuth-gated MCP servers via the workbench (copilot parity)

An OAuth-gated http MCP server (e.g. the eng-hub server at mcp.eng.ms)
reached codex but failed to start with "not logged in", because codex
won't expose an unauthenticated server's tools. The Copilot agent makes
the same server work by reporting it as `AuthRequired`, letting the
workbench acquire an OAuth bearer token (VS Code dynamic client
registration), and injecting that token into the connection. Bring the
same mechanism to codex.

- Detect the auth failure: a `failed` `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated`
  whose error indicates sign-in is required now surfaces as
  `McpServerStatus.AuthRequired` (with the server URL as the OAuth
  `resource`) via the shared `McpCustomizationController`, so the
  workbench renders the same "Authenticate" affordance it uses for
  Copilot.
- Receive the token: implement `IAgent.handleAuthenticationToken` on the
  codex agent. When the workbench completes sign-in, the fanned-out
  `authenticate` command delivers the bearer; codex stores it keyed by
  the normalized server URL (process-global, so it applies to every
  session/thread on the shared app-server).
- Inject + reconnect: `_buildSessionMcpServers` adds
  `http_headers.Authorization: Bearer <token>` for any server with a
  stored token. Affected threads reconnect -- a pre-first-turn thread is
  restarted (lossless), one with history resumes with the current
  `config.mcp_servers` on its next turn (`thread/resume` carries the same
  `config` field). Verified against the real codex binary: it forwards
  `http_headers` on every MCP HTTP request, so a 401-gated server is
  rejected without the bearer and connects (exposing its tools) with it.

New pure, unit-tested helpers in codexMcpServers.ts:
`normalizeCodexMcpResourceUrl`, `codexStartupErrorNeedsAuth`,
`injectCodexMcpAuthTokens`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: discover MCP OAuth metadata so the workbench Authenticate action works

Clicking "Authenticate" on an auth-gated codex MCP server (e.g. via MCP:
List Servers) did nothing: the workbench's `resolveMcpServerAuthentication`
iterates `ProtectedResourceMetadata.authorization_servers` and returns
early when it is empty, and the metadata codex synthesized carried only
`{ resource, resource_name }`. codex's `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated`
failure omits the RFC 9728 challenge, so unlike the Copilot SDK (which
discovers the metadata internally) we had no authorization server to sign
in against.

Discover it: when surfacing an auth-gated server as `AuthRequired`, fetch
its Protected Resource Metadata from
`<url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (base `fetchResourceMetadata`,
15s timeout) and carry the resulting `authorization_servers` +
`scopes_supported` in the `AuthRequired` state. The workbench then runs the
exact same OAuth (dynamic client registration -> browser sign-in) it uses
for Copilot, and the acquired bearer flows back through
`handleAuthenticationToken`. Discovery failure still surfaces `AuthRequired`
with bare metadata (the server genuinely needs auth) and is logged.

This makes `_handleMcpStartupStatus` -> auth handling asynchronous: the
server stays in its prior (starting) state until discovery resolves, then
settles into `AuthRequired`. Verified the discovery step against the
compiled base helper (well-known PRM doc -> authorization_servers).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: harden MCP config/auth handling and fix a Windows-only test

Addresses review feedback on the MCP integration plus a cross-platform
test bug:

- Fix Windows unit test: `codexSkillRootsFromPlugins` returns native
  fsPaths (backslashes on Windows), so the test now derives the expected
  roots via the same `URI.file(...).fsPath` transform instead of a
  hardcoded posix path. (This was the failing `Windows / Electron` check.)

- Route auth tokens by OAuth resource, not server URL: RFC 9728 discovery
  can return a `resource` that differs from the configured server endpoint
  (e.g. root `https://host/` for a `https://host/mcp` server). We now
  record a resource -> server-URL association when surfacing `AuthRequired`
  and resolve the pushed token through it (keeping a direct-URL fallback),
  so the bearer is injected for the right server even when they differ.

- Re-prompt on a rejected token: an expired/revoked/insufficient-scope
  token previously suppressed `AuthRequired` and became a terminal error
  with no way to re-auth. A repeated auth failure now clears the stored
  token and re-surfaces `AuthRequired`.

- Sanitize untrusted server config: `args`/`env`/`http_headers` values are
  coerced to the string shapes codex requires (and non-string `cwd`
  dropped), so a malformed Host Settings entry can't make codex reject the
  whole per-thread config.

- Strip a pre-existing case-insensitive `authorization` header before
  injecting the bearer, so a configured lowercase `authorization` can't
  leave a stale credential alongside the injected one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix duplicate read/write permission prompts in Copilot agent (#324477) (#326030)

The Copilot CLI runtime emits two identical `permission.requested` events
for a single file read or write (an internal `path` prompt followed by a
`read`/`write` prompt). The SDK hides `promptRequest` from the handler, so
the agent host saw two byte-identical requests for the same tool call and
prompted the user to approve the same operation twice.

Cache the signature of a user-approved read/write request keyed by tool
call id and auto-approve exactly one subsequent byte-identical request.
The grant is single-use and cleared on tool completion, client-tool
completion, and pending-permission teardown, so approval never carries
across a different tool call, changed path/diff/contents, or a different
permission kind.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: move read/unread ownership to sessions providers (#325982)

* sessions: move read/unread ownership to sessions providers

Marking a session read/unread is now done by the sessions provider
(surfaced via ISession.isRead) instead of the UI-layer
SessionsListModelService. Existing locally-stored read state is migrated
once into provider ownership.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: address read/unread migration review feedback

Consolidate read state onto ISession.isRead as the single source of truth: drop the display-only isSessionRead override and instead persist the active session as read from the sessions service, so the list and header both read the provider-owned flag directly.

Mark AgentHost sessions unread on cancelled and errored turns too, matching the Copilot and local-chat providers so a background session that errors or is cancelled while unwatched shows as unread.

Also trims verbose migration comments across the touched files.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: address read/unread group and migration review feedback

- Local and Copilot providers now mark read/unread across every chat in a
  group, not just the primary, so a session with an unread child can be
  cleared via Mark as Read.
- Local sessions persisted before `isRead` existed now load as unread so the
  additive migration can promote genuinely-read legacy sessions.
- Local first-chat model tracking is installed before awaiting turn
  completion, so a background completion/error marks the session unread even
  if the user navigates away mid-turn.
- Update SESSIONS_LIST.md to describe the actual read/unread data flow.
- Drop an unnecessary timeout in the agent-side-effects persistence test.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: provide isRead on the SessionHeader fixture mock session

The session header now reads the provider-owned `session.isRead` observable
directly, so the fixture's mock session must supply it — otherwise the
component fixture throws while rendering.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Phase 10.6: MCP elicitation (real `onElicitation` translation) (#325908)

* Phase 10.6: MCP elicitation (real onElicitation translation)

Replace the Phase-7 `onElicitation` cancel-stub with a real translation.
When an MCP server calls `elicit/create`, the request now surfaces to the
user as structured input (a `ChatInputRequested` form/URL prompt, the same
channel `AskUserQuestion` uses — not the permission gate) instead of being
silently auto-cancelled, and the answer is delivered back to the server as
an `ElicitResult`.

- New `claudeElicitation.ts`: pure projections (schema -> questions,
  answers -> content). Each field is runtime-validated with the base-layer
  `validation.ts`, the field type is derived from that validator, and pinned
  to the MCP SDK's `PrimitiveSchemaDefinition` by a compile-time guard.
- New `claudeElicitationBridge.ts`: `handleElicitation` parks on
  `requestUserInput`, observes the SDK abort signal, and maps the response
  back to an `ElicitResult` (decline only for an explicit user Decline;
  no-session / teardown / abort -> cancel).
- Wire `onElicitation` through `IBuildOptionsInput` / `IMaterializeContext` /
  `ClaudeAgent._makeOnElicitation`, mirroring `canUseTool`; remove the
  `logElicitation` stub.
- form + url modes; Phase-7 Test 18 stub replaced with the real translation;
  extensive projection + bridge + agent-level + integration coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Phase 10.6: address PR review — correctness fixes vs the workbench consumer

Copilot review surfaced real gaps against agentHostSessionHandler.ts:

- Schema-aware answer coercion: the consumer renders number/integer/boolean
  questions as text inputs and returns text answers, so coerce "3"/"false"
  back to 3/false per the field type (uncoercible values dropped).
- Disable free-form input on strict MCP enum/select questions (the consumer
  defaults allowFreeformInput to true, allowing out-of-schema values that
  the translator would silently drop).
- Cancel question-less requests instead of falsely accepting: a url-mode
  request missing its URL, or a form with no representable fields, otherwise
  becomes the consumer's injected required text question and resolves as
  accept. The bridge now cancels a request with neither a URL nor questions.
- Prototype-pollution safety: read answers with Object.hasOwn and build
  content via Object.fromEntries so an untrusted `__proto__`/`constructor`
  field name can't read an inherited member (crash) or mutate the prototype.
- Docs: correct the drift-guard docstring (catches incompatible reshapes,
  not additive new variants); drop the out-of-scope SDKElicitationComplete
  router bullet from the roadmap; reconcile stale test-count notes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: keep new-session config chips visible (disabled) while a draft re-resolves (#325953)

* sessions: keep new-session config chips visible (disabled) while a draft re-resolves

Switching workspace or agent in the new-session composer creates a fresh
draft whose config schema is momentarily empty, which blanked the isolation
and branch chips until the resolve landed. Cache the well-known config-property
schemas and re-inject them (disabled) during the resolve so the chips stay put
and re-enable with resolved values, instead of disappearing and reappearing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* sessions: move new-draft schema cache to the provider so it survives toolbar rebuilds

PR review pointed out the cache lived on the AgentHostSessionConfigPicker action
view item, which the toolbar disposes and recreates when the NewSessionRepositoryConfig
menu re-evaluates on a session-type switch (its isolation/branch items gate on
SessionTypeContext). The recreated picker started with an empty cache, so the
chips still blanked.

Move the well-known schema cache onto BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider (a long-lived
singleton) and seed new drafts via initialConfigSchema, so getSessionConfig returns
the isolation/branch chips immediately and any freshly-created picker renders them
(disabled) during the resolve. Revert the picker-side cache. Add a provider test for
the seeding and rework the DOM test to exercise an actual picker recreation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
sessions: avoid force-opening managed tabs when opening a file in single-pane layout (#325865)

* sessions: do not force-open managed tabs when opening a file in single-pane layout

Rework the single-pane managed docked tabs (Changes + Files placeholder) so
they are only opened into an *empty* editor group on a view-open trigger,
removing the fragile dismissal bookkeeping and aux-bar-visibility inference.

- Add layout-service events `onDidRevealSidePane` (side pane goes fully
  hidden -> visible) and `onDidEndSessionLayoutRestore` (restore epoch settles)
  and drive the managed-tabs strategy off named triggers A-D.
- Open default tabs only when the group is empty, so closing a managed tab
  sticks and closing a file no longer re-forces the tabs open / leaves the
  side pane un-closable.
- Ensure Changes (opened active) on new-session submit; ensure all docked
  inputs on a details-only reveal.
- Scope pending reconcile intents to their session so a superseded reconcile
  cannot leak its intent onto a switched-to session.
- Gate responsive sessions-list auto-collapse on small windows (<= 1800px).
- Only collapse editors on a details-only hide (aux still visible), not when
  the whole side pane closes.
- Tests + docs (SINGLE_PANE_SCENARIOS.md, sessions SKILL.md) updated.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: address CCR review feedback on single-pane managed tabs

- Guard the Files-tab tidy on onWillOpenEditor: resolve the event group via
  mainPart.getGroup and skip re-activations (already-open editors) and
  non-main-part groups, so selecting/closing-to-reveal an existing file no
  longer removes a user-added Files tab.
- Open the submit Changes tab with preserveFocus so activating it for detail
  mapping never steals focus from the just-submitted chat.
- Remove the now-dead internallyClosingEditors bookkeeping from the coordinator

commit.message:
editor: consolidate diff-editor command handlers into IDiffEditorCommandsService (#325869)

Follow-up to #325382. Move the remaining inline diff-editor command
handlers (open side, next/previous change, focus side, toggle
ignore-trim-whitespace, swap sides) out of diffEditorCommands.ts and
into IDiffEditorCommandsService, matching the delegation pattern already
used for toggleRenderSideBySide. Each command handler now delegates to
the service via accessor.get(IDiffEditorCommandsService).

Services are injected in the service constructor instead of resolved
via ServicesAccessor inside the handlers, and methods that perform
config writes are async so failures propagate to the caller. The
getActiveTextDiffEditor/getActiveDiffModifiedResource resolver helpers
are now private methods on the service since they have no external
callers. The Agents window override (SessionsDiffEditorCommandsService)
still only overrides toggleRenderSideBySide and inherits the rest.

Adds unit tests for the newly consolidated service methods.

commit.message:
Collapse Agent Host per-session GitHub token map to the singleton token

The restricted telemetry router kept a per-session `_githubTokensBySdkSession`
map so each forwarded event could resolve its identity from the token its
session launched with. VS Code only ever sources a single `_githubToken` and
snapshots that same value into every session, so the map added lifecycle
plumbing (register/rollback plus clear/delete across every launch and teardown
path) without changing behavior today. Resolve the restricted telemetry
context from `this._githubToken` directly and drop the map.

The runtime still supports per-session tokens and live credential swaps, but
VS Code does not exercise that path (no `setCredentials`), so a divergent
per-session token cannot occur here. The no-token / BYOK case stays fail-safe:
no token means no restricted telemetry.

commit.message:
Voice: show "Answered" instead of "Skipped" for externally-answered questions (#325698)

* Voice: show "Answered" instead of "Skipped" for externally-answered questions

When a question carousel is answered outside its own UI (e.g. a voice or
free-text response the model interprets), the agent host completes the input
request with Accept but no structured answers, so the summary rendered
"Skipped" even though the user did respond.

Track the completion outcome and mark the carousel answeredExternally when it
is accepted without structured answers, then render "Answered" in the summary.

Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8157

* address feedback

commit.message:
sessions: fix list_sessions returning 0 for status:['archived'] (#325749)

* sessions: fix list_sessions returning 0 for status:['archived']

The default archived-exclusion in filterSessions unconditionally hid
archived sessions unless includeArchived was also passed, even when
the caller explicitly asked for status: ['archived']. This made it
impossible to list Done/completed sessions via list_sessions without
also passing includeArchived: true.

Also fix the status name matching to consider sessionIsArchived's
metadata flag (session.isArchived), not just the SessionStatus bit,
so sessions archived only via the metadata flag are found by
status: ['archived'] too.

Update the status field's tool description to clarify that archived
corresponds to Done/completed sessions.

Fixes #325605

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: use one status decoder for filtering and serialization

Address review feedback on PR #325749: the synthesized 'archived'
name added to fix status:['archived'] filtering was only used during
filtering. serializeSession still derived the returned status solely
from session.status, so a metadata-only archived session (no
SessionStatus.IsArchived bit) was filtered in as archived but
serialized with a stale status (e.g. 'idle') or none at all.

Unify the two paths: describeSessionStatusNames(session) now decodes
both the SessionStatus bit-flags and the isArchived metadata flag,
and is used by both filterSessions and serializeSession (via the new
describeSessionStatus(session) wrapper) so the reported status is
consistent with the filtering result.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

skipped trailing lowered code units. Iterate over queryLower.length instead

commit.message:
sessions: fix docked detail panel gap at bottom in single-pane layout (#325863)

* sessions: fix docked detail panel leaving a gap at the bottom in single-pane layout

The single-pane auxiliary bar renders no title strip (the single tab bar
lives on the editor part) but inherited `hasTitle: true` from the base
auxiliary bar. `PartLayout` still subtracted the title height from the
content area, so the docked detail panel content was laid out ~35px short,
leaving an empty gap at the bottom.

Clear `hasTitle` in `create()` so the content fills the full docked
rectangle, and drop the now-redundant `createTitleArea` override.

commit.message:
Claude agent: allow 'max' reasoning effort on the runtime path (#325851)

* Claude agent: allow 'max' reasoning effort on the runtime path

The SDK's `Settings.effortLevel` type (reused by `applyFlagSettings`) omits 'max', so `clampEffortForRuntime` degraded a mid-session 'max' selection to 'xhigh'. But the Anthropic API / Copilot CAPI accept 'max' end-to-end (confirmed with Anthropic; verified a 'max' turn round-trips with output_config.effort=max on the /v1/messages call). Pass 'max' through via a single contained cast, keeping the narrow ClaudeRuntimeEffortLevel return type so downstream consumers stay honest against the SDK's declared surface. Also drops the now-incorrect 'max'->'xhigh' warning in setModel.

SDK typing issue: anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript#377

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rename clampEffortForRuntime -> toRuntimeEffortLevel

The function no longer clamps ('max' now passes through), so the old name was misleading. Behavior is unchanged; this is a pure rename. Addresses PR review feedback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Forward mid-turn Claude permissionMode changes to the live SDK (#321691) (#325726)

* Forward mid-turn Claude permissionMode changes to the live SDK (#321691)

Changing a Claude agent-host session's approvals mid-turn (e.g. "Ask
Before Edits" -> "Bypass Permissions") only reached the SDK at the next
send(), so the SDK kept prompting for the rest of the in-flight turn.

Add `onDidSessionConfigChange` to `IAgentConfigurationService` (fired
from the `SessionConfigChanged` envelope, symmetric with
`onDidRootConfigChange`), and have `ClaudeAgent` forward the new
`permissionMode` to the live `Query` via `setPermissionMode`. This is
the SDK-owned equivalent of the host-owned `autoApprove` axis, which
already applies mid-turn via `getAutoApproval`.

Fire-and-forget so the SDK control request never interleaves with a
parked `canUseTool`; no-op until the session is materialized.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: only forward client-originated permissionMode changes

Copilot review found that the previous version also fired for the
internal `permissionMode` write in `handleExitPlanMode`, which runs
inside a still-open `canUseTool` callback — issuing a live
`setPermissionMode` there can deadlock the turn (claudeCanUseTool.ts).

- Gate the live forward on `isClientOriginated`: only user/picker
  (client-dispatched) changes reach the SDK; internal server writes
  (ExitPlanMode) are left for the next `send()` as before.
- Emit post-reducer merged `values` instead of the raw patch so a merge
  and a full `replace` are reported uniformly to consumers.
- Rework the regression test to dispatch both a server write (ignored)
  and a client write (forwarded) mid-turn, and condense its comments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Refactor: forward via IAgent.onSessionConfigChanged instead of an origin flag

Replaces the `onDidSessionConfigChange` event + `isClientOriginated` flag
with a structural distinction: the picker's config change is the only
`SessionConfigChanged` that reaches `agentSideEffects.handleAction` (server-
side writes like ExitPlanMode use `dispatchServerAction` and never route
there). Forward from that client-only path via a new optional
`IAgent.onSessionConfigChanged(session, values)` hook, mirroring
`onArchivedChanged`.

- Remove the config-service event and the payload flag.
- ClaudeAgent implements the hook to forward `permissionMode` to the live SDK.
- Add agentSideEffects coverage that the hook receives the post-reducer
  merged values, and retarget the Claude regression test to the hook.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review: revert per-session fan-out, apply fallback on permissionMode deletion

- permissionMode is the live Query's mode and each chat has its own Query, and
  the picker dispatches to the session URI (the default chat) — so forward to
  the single chat the change is scoped to (resolved from the channel), not
  every chat in the session (which would clobber unchanged chats).
- A `replace` that deletes permissionMode now resolves to the same
  `permissionModeFallback` the next `send()` would apply, so live state mirrors
  the reducer instead of keeping the old mode; covered by a mid-turn test.
- Strengthen the agentSideEffects test to seed an untouched key and assert it
  survives, pinning that the hook receives merged values, not the raw patch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Apply mid-turn permissionMode to every chat in the session (matches Copilot)

permissionMode is a session-scoped config value today (AHP has no per-chat
config), so a picker change should reach every materialized chat's Query, not
just the one the change arrived on — matching Copilot's session-scoped
approvals. Fan out `onSessionConfigChanged` over `entry.allChatSessions()`.

TODO to scope per-chat once the protocol supports it, tracked at
microsoft/agent-host-protocol#335.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
agent host e2e: reuse one replay server per suite for Copilot (#325410)

* agent host e2e: reuse one replay server per suite for Copilot

The agent host e2e replay suite restarted the whole server (and re-spawned
the provider SDK/CLI subprocess) for every test. Profiling showed the
dominant per-test cost is server fork (~0.5s) plus the provider SDK client
cold start (~0.5s, an ~8MB CLI bundle loaded on the Electron-as-node
binary), with session teardown effectively free.

Reuse one server across the suite for providers that can be returned to a
clean state via disposeSession, swapping the per-test replay fixture on the
in-process CapiReplayProxy without restarting (the proxy URL the agent host
was forked against stays fixed):

- CapiReplayProxy: add resetForReplay (re-point at a new fixture, clear
  replay buckets + cache-miss log), assertNoCacheMisses (verify strict
  replay without stopping), and close (drop the socket without the strict
  check). stop() now composes these.
- Add AgentHostE2EServerLease to encapsulate per-test vs shared strategies,
  gated by a new supportsSharedReplayServer provider flag (replay only;
  recording always uses a fresh proxy + fixture per test).
- Enable it for Copilot. Claude stays per-test: its mid-turn dispose can
  wedge the shared agent host process, which per-test kill-and-refork
  isolation guards against.
- Drain the permission test's post-tool continuation to turnComplete in all
  modes so the session ends cleanly before dispose (returning mid-turn would
  wedge the reused client).

Copilot suite drops from ~29s to ~14s mocha time. Claude and Codex are
unchanged (per-test path).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent host e2e: address Copilot review feedback

- CapiReplayProxy: route the constructor's fixture-existence check and error
  message through this._fixturePath so all fixture-path access has a single
  source of truth.
- AgentHostE2EServerLease.acquire: fail fast with a clear error instead of a
  non-null assertion when a shared server unexpectedly has no capiReplay proxy.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent host e2e: document the shared replay server in the README

Add a "Server lifecycle" section covering the per-test vs shared strategies,
how AgentHostE2EServerLease and CapiReplayProxy.resetForReplay swap fixtures
without restarting (in-process, no IPC), why sharing is opt-in per provider
(Copilot yes, Claude no), and the "don't return mid-turn" rule for authors.
Also add the supportsSharedReplayServer gate row, list the lease in the
components table, and add a troubleshooting entry for cross-test state leaks.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent host e2e: enable the shared replay server for Claude and Codex

Investigated the long-standing "Claude mid-turn dispose wedges the agent
host" caveat that kept server reuse Copilot-only. It dates from the live
real-SDK era (real streaming turns actually in flight). In today's
deterministic replay suite there is no mid-turn dispose: the abort test is
record-only and every turn drains to `turnComplete` before teardown.

Deliberately reproducing the old failure (reverting the permission test's
drain) showed it is not a process wedge at all but a strict cache miss: an
undrained turn's continuation HTTP call fires after the fixture is swapped
and lands in the next test's window as an unrecorded call. The proxy detects
it loudly. The cure is exactly the drain already in place, so with every turn
drained there is nothing to leak.

Enable `supportsSharedReplayServer` for Claude and Codex (verified green and
stable across repeated runs; Claude ~16s -> ~9s, Codex likewise). Correct the
drain rationale and the README/lease/flag comments to describe the real
mechanism (leaked async traffic) instead of the "wedge" folklore.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent host e2e: drop supportsSharedReplayServer, share by default in replay

The flag was true for all three providers, so it modeled the wrong thing: a
per-provider capability, when the real requirement is a per-test invariant
(drain your turns) that every provider already meets. Server reuse is really
a property of replay mode, gated only by recording (which needs a fresh proxy
per fixture).

Remove the flag and make the lease share by default in replay
(`_shared = !RECORD`). No behavior change (all three suites already reused the
server); this just deletes dead config and the misleading "some providers
can't share" framing. Single-test isolation for diagnosing a cross-test leak
is still available via `--grep`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
build: support platform-specific built-in extensions from GitHub releases (#324206)

* Support platform-specific built-in extensions from GitHub releases

Adds support for downloading platform-specific built-in extension VSIXs
from GitHub releases, keyed by marketplace target platform. Also downloads
the latest pre-release assets for insiders builds, ignoring the pinned
version and checksum.

- extensionTarget.ts: resolve build target + release asset name
- builtInExtensions.ts: platformSpecific checksum map + insiders detection
- extensions.ts/fetch.ts: fromGithub asset selection + prerelease support
- CI: platform-aware cache key and target env plumbing

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Insiders downloads the latest release instead of latest pre-release

sessions: show Submit Feedback action in the single-pane Changes editor (#325753)

The agent-feedback overlay resolves a session's changed files from the
active editor via getActiveResourceCandidates, which only unwrapped a

Changes editor is a SessionChangesEditorInput that wraps the multi-diff
input, so the file URIs could not be resolved and the Submit Feedback
action stayed hidden. Expose the wrapped input and unwrap it during

commit.message:
Push BYOK models to the agent host instead of pulling them (#325737)

* agentHost: push BYOK models over onDidChangeModels

Change the reverse BYOK LM bridge from a pull model to a push model. The
renderer now owns its model set and pushes the current snapshot over
`onDidChangeModels` (on subscribe and on every change) instead of answering
`listModels()` round-trips. `IByokLmBridgeConnection.onDidChangeModels` becomes
required and carries `IByokLmModelInfo[]`; the client channel serves a snapshot
stream that enumerates renderer-locally and drops `listModels`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: cache pushed BYOK snapshots in the bridge registry

Subscribe to each connection's onDidChangeModels on register and cache the
pushed snapshot rather than enumerating connections. A connection becomes
serving once it pushes its first snapshot (even empty). Drop listModels and the
per-connection re-enumeration path from the registry.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: read BYOK session models from the registry cache

Read the serving window's models from the registry's cache of renderer-pushed
snapshots. The renderer pushes on connect, so the cache is warm by session-create
time; drop the preferCache parameter and the live-enumeration fallback.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: update BYOK tests for the push model

Rework the BYOK tests to drive connections by pushing model snapshots over
onDidChangeModels instead of scripting listModels, and assert against the
registry cache. Non-serving windows are modeled as connections that never push.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: implement throttling for BYOK model snapshot emissions

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
